interpretations.statement: The confirmation reproduced the component pattern and refuted the speed magnitude. It returned valid_failure with accepted false, while execution completeness, evaluation validity, task evaluator, force bounds, solver errors, holding coverage, evaluator task bound, holding position 0.005873395025975773 m and terminal error 0.00415282329502572 m all passed and holding speed 0.21090377835105664 m/s failed against the 0.02 m/s limit. Against the original execution of the same configuration (0.004975039037709839 m, 0.0027978634541274573 m, 0.09248004936026318 m/s) the structural conclusion that segment material stiffness removes the T2 holding-position and terminal violations is confirmed, the configuration is confirmed to be exactly one acceptance component short of a pass, and the earlier 12.1x speed-reduction claim is refuted: the identical configuration moved 2.3x in holding speed with unchanged seed, weights, structure and solver settings.

interpretations.scope: Whole study, including the identical-configuration pair (sealed execution and this fresh exact confirmation).
interpretations.statement: Identical configurations are not reproducible to better than a factor of about 2.3 in holding_max_speed under this protocol, with zero solver errors and no setting change. This bounds the campaign's resolving power: single-execution differences of tens of percent in that metric are not attributable to configuration, so the fine-grained T2 holding-weight comparison across 0.88-1.22 m/s, and any cross-template weight-transfer inference at that granularity, are not reliable evidence about the weights themselves.
interpretations.uncertainty: Measured on one metric at one configuration, so it must not be generalised to other metrics (holding position reproduced within 18% between the same two executions) or to other templates, and the mechanism of the variability is unidentified.

final_model_decision.reasoning:
Final disposition of the first bounded Mainline5 study, submitted as the closing STOP that consumes the returned fresh exact confirmation. The current feedback is the verification report (status verification_completed); the confirmed configuration is the selected incumbent batch-fbd248186774fdd1-0, and the result is reported as returned, failure included.

Fresh confirmation, reported plainly. The confirmed configuration is the stiff-material T2 incumbent: all three segment material scenarios stiff, section and routing radius scales 1.0, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.05, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.1. Its fresh exact execution returned valid_failure with accepted false, passing evaluation validity, execution completeness, task evaluator, evaluator task bound, force bounds, solver errors and holding coverage, passing holding position 0.005873395025975773 m and terminal error 0.00415282329502572 m, and failing holding speed 0.21090377835105664 m/s against the 0.02 m/s limit. Against the original execution of the same configuration (holding position 0.004975039037709839 m, terminal error 0.0027978634541274573 m, holding speed 0.09248004936026318 m/s) the component structure reproduced and the speed magnitude did not: the same configuration moved 2.3x in holding speed with unchanged seed, weights, structure and solver settings. The configuration is therefore confirmed as a valid, non-accepting incumbent that is exactly one acceptance component short of a pass, and the earlier claim of a specific 12.1x stiffness-driven speed reduction is withdrawn as a magnitude.

Methods actually used, and what was not used. Explicit one-factor enumeration of the holding_tip_speed_weight domain on T2 at baseline stiffness; explicit one-factor enumeration of the segment material scenario at anchored control weights; one fresh exact confirmation of the selected incumbent. No coordinate search, smoothing, interpolation, mathematical analysis tool or worker call grounded any conclusion. Direct transfer from T0 was tested rather than discussed: the Mainline4-selected pair 0.0375/0.1 failed on T2 at baseline stiffness with holding_max_error 0.023420466402621826 m and holding_max_speed 1.2169348820640329 m/s, which is the worst speed among the four baseline-stiffness weights.

Valid physical outcomes and improvement against a reference. All seven executions on T2 are valid and complete outcomes with zero solver errors, zero force-bound violations and full inclusive holding coverage. Against the sealed baseline-material T2 point at identical control weights, the stiff structure improves holding position from 0.023420466402621826 m to 0.004975039037709839 m and again 0.005873395025975773 m (a confirmed pass, roughly 4x), terminal error from 0.0033639419880512693 m to 0.0027978634541274573 and 0.00415282329502572 m (passing in both), and holding speed from 0.8825765295566194 m/s to 0.09248004936026318 and 0.21090377835105664 m/s, a 4x to 10x improvement that is unstable and remains 4.6x to 10.5x above the limit. The compliant-material configuration is worse on all three components (0.03145144587408842 m, 0.13345246457739318 m/s, 0.030191067901434228 m) and is the only T2 point failing the terminal bound, so the material axis is monotone at scenario level.

Supporting and weakening evidence, and unknowns. Supporting: the exact transfer failure; the bit-identical holding error at 0.023420466402621826 m across five control weights at baseline stiffness; the reproduced passes of holding position and terminal reach at stiff stiffness; the monotone compliant-baseline-stiff ordering; and the clean validity of every execution including the confirmation. Weakening: the 2.3x run-to-run spread in holding speed bounds the campaign's resolving power, so fine-grained weight comparisons and cross-template weight inferences at that granularity are not reliable; the stiffness finding rests on two executions of one configuration and one of the opposite extreme; material scenarios multiply only the Young modulus while retaining density and bending viscosity, so stiffness and damping cannot be separated; the authorized geometry levers were never executed; the development allocation, not scientific preference, ended the search; all executions are compute-bound with all thirty-five control deadlines missed and roughly 21-23 s mean update; and cross-template differences in force capacity, guide/routing and tension initialization prevent attributing the transfer failure to geometry alone. Unknowns carried forward: why holding speed varies 2.3x while holding position reproduces within 18%; whether the geometry levers can close the residual holding-speed violation; whether holding_tip_speed_weight becomes effective once the structure is stiff; whether the compliant terminal failure marks a different regime; and how T3 behaves under structural change.

Findings and procedures worth carrying forward, with scope. (1) On T2 with controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0, the frozen 0.35 s duration and 0.05 s holding window, holding_tip_speed_weight in [0.025, 0.1] is inert for holding position at baseline stiffness and cannot reach the holding-speed limit. (2) Segment material stiffness is the first-order lever on the T2 holding failure: stiff converts the holding-position and terminal violations into passes and leaves a speed-only violation, compliant degrades all three; scope is two numerical scenarios, single seed, no validated materials. (3) The Mainline4 T0 weight prescription does not transfer to the three-segment template; scope is one transferred pair. (4) Identical configurations are not reproducible to better than about 2.3x in holding speed under this protocol, so single-execution differences below that factor must not be read as configuration effects. (5) Practical procedure: structural mutations must be built from a contemporary candidate.family@2.0.0 configuration, since the mainline3-era artifact carries no semantic decision block and a source without T2 context rejects the middle segment.

Explicit non-claims. No robustness, no real-time capability, no global or template-level optimality, no universal weight or stiffness law, no claim that T2 can or cannot pass under the untested geometry levers, no claim about T3 beyond its baseline failure, and no completion of Mainline5 or Mainline6. The study closes on the fixed template T2 with a tested-and-failed direct transfer from T0, an evidenced control-domain exhaustion at baseline stiffness, a confirmed-but-non-accepting structural effect whose reproducible components and non-reproducible speed magnitude are distinguished, one verified non-accepted incumbent, unused geometry levers and T3 as documented unknowns, and a quantified reproducibility limit for the protocol. No retry-to-pass was performed and no sealed configuration was re-run.

factual_annotations.review: A finite contrast cannot eliminate other authorized geometry/control values or establish a mechanism. This activity fixes T2 once selected; no T3 execution was authorized by a subsequent plan.

factual_annotations.claim: Stiff improves speed by 9.5x against an identical-weight 0.8825765295566194 m/s baseline; compliant degrades every component.
factual_annotations.review: The actual material runs use 0.05/0.1. Their identified historical T2 baseline speed is 1.1210197701767821 m/s, not the contemporary 0.025 baseline 0.8825765295566194. Stiff development speed is about 12.12x lower. Compliant worsens position and terminal error but improves speed to 0.13345246457739318; it is a trade-off, not worsening of all components. Material speed response is not monotone across compliant/baseline/stiff.

factual_annotations.claim: The baseline holding error was stiffness-limited rather than a window-boundary artifact.
factual_annotations.review: Changing numerical Young modulus changes the recorded closed-loop trajectory. This demonstrates sample-level sensitivity, but does not independently identify the physical or timing mechanism or eliminate a holding-window boundary explanation.

factual_annotations.claim: Structural mutations require a contemporary source because historical T2 lacks semantic decisions.
factual_annotations.review: The accepted material plan actually used historical v2-T2. The repaired failure was an inactive middle-parameter comparison on other two-segment historical templates. The finite-template projection derives semantic decisions from the fixed catalog and preserves historical source identity; contemporary-only sourcing is not established.

factual_annotations.claim: Two same-configuration speeds define a 2.3x protocol reproducibility limit or minimum effect threshold.
factual_annotations.review: 0.09248004936026318 and 0.21090377835105664 m/s are two observed nominal results, not a statistical precision bound. They do not establish a universal resolving power, variance or threshold below which configuration effects are impossible.
